title: Mitchell Starc Becomes All-Time Leading Left-Arm Test Wicket-Taker, Equals Kapil Dev
excerpt: The Australian pace spearhead surpassed Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath and drew level with Indian legend Kapil Dev's career tally of 434 Test wickets during the first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin.
body:
• Mitchell Starc surpassed Rangana Herath's 433 wickets to become the highest wicket-taking left-arm bowler in Test cricket history
  • With 434 wickets, Starc has drawn level with Indian great Kapil Dev and needs just one more to surpass the former India captain's career tally
  • The 36-year-old is also closing in on Dale Steyn's 439 wickets, which would place him fifth among the all-time highest wicket-taking fast bowlers

Mitchell Starc etched his name into Test cricket history during the first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, surpassing Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath to become the highest wicket-taking left-arm bowler in the format's history. The milestone also saw the Australian left-armer draw level with Indian legend Kapil Dev on 434 Test wickets.

Surpassing Herath

Starc had equalled Herath's record of 433 Test wickets during the fifth Ashes Test at the Sydney Cricket Ground earlier this year, where he claimed 31 wickets across the series as Australia secured a 4-1 triumph over England. His first wicket in the Bangladesh innings at Marrara Stadium in Darwin took him to 434, making him the outright leading left-arm bowler in Test history.

https://x.com/Cricketracker/status/2087797240203284602

Herath, a wily Sri Lankan spinner, accumulated his 433 wickets across 93 Tests between 1999 and 2018. Starc reached the same mark in 105 Tests but as a pace bowler, a fundamentally different discipline that places significantly greater physical strain on the body.

The Kapil Dev Milestone

For Indian cricket fans, the more resonant milestone is Starc's arrival at 434 wickets, which places him level with Kapil Dev, one of India's most revered all-rounders. The former India captain took 434 wickets across 131 Tests and remains the only cricketer to score over 5,000 runs and take more than 400 wickets in the format.

While the wicket tallies are now level, statistical comparisons reveal the depth of Kapil Dev's legacy. The Indian legend recorded 23 five-wicket hauls compared to Starc's 18, and bowled 1,060 maiden overs against Starc's 622, demonstrating a level of sustained control that few fast bowlers have matched, according to India Bytes.

"It means I've played a bit. It is cool and very humbling to be spoken about with those guys. But that stuff doesn't mean a whole lot while you're still playing. You don't get too far ahead."

— Mitchell Starc, speaking to AAP

A Late-Career Renaissance

What makes Starc's achievement remarkable is the timing. The 36-year-old has enjoyed the most prolific stretch of his career in recent years, claiming 55 Test wickets at an average of 17.32 in the past year alone, according to cricket.com.au. He credits improved mental clarity and the stability of Australia's pace attack, working alongside captain Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood, for his sustained form.

"Excuse my language, but it's just been letting shit go," Starc told the Australian Associated Press. "You're never as good or bad as you think or other people think you are."

Since turning 35, only Australian great Glenn McGrath has taken more Test wickets among the country's fast bowlers. Starc's technical evolution, particularly his use of the wobble seam with the Kookaburra ball, has also been a factor in maintaining his threat across different conditions.

What Comes Next

The immediate target is surpassing Kapil Dev, which would require just one more wicket in the ongoing Darwin Test. Beyond that, South African legend Dale Steyn's 439 wickets are within reach. Seven wickets across the two-Test Bangladesh series would take Starc past Steyn and into fifth place among the highest wicket-taking fast bowlers in Test history, behind only James Anderson (704), Stuart Broad (604), Glenn McGrath (563) and Courtney Walsh (519).

The Bangladesh series also carries World Test Championship significance. Australia are fielding a full-strength squad including Cummins, Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, with the second Test scheduled in Mackay from August 22 to 26. For Indian fans tracking the WTC standings, Australia's results in this series will have direct implications for India's path to the final.
